newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Sempati Air preparing for 1997 float.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Sempati Air preparing for 1997 float.

text.p: Indonesia's privately owned PT Sempati Air has undergone a management shake-up to prepare it for a public listing next year, the official Antara news agency said on Wednesday.

"The changes in Sempati's directors, besides anticipating plans to go public, are to raise the company's performance in order that it can compete, not just with domestic firms but also with foreign ones," Sempati's president commissioner, Hutomo Mandala Putra, was quoted as saying.

Mandala Putra, President Suharto's youngest son, said the changes in the directors were made to increase the firm's consolidation and efficiency. They included replacing the company's president director, Hasan Sujono, with Santun Nainggolan.
Indonesia's only credit rating agency, PT Pefindo, earlier this month took the unprecedented step of placing a ratings alert on commercial paper issued by Sempati.
Pefindo said it took the move because of Sempati's "deteriorating financial performance of late, particularly on its liquidity and leverage conditions".
The airline's weak financial position was widely blamed for the postponment of the long-planned float from October 1996.

Sempati's shareholders are Asian Aviation Inc, a Malaysian-Indonesian joint venture with a 40 percent stake, timber tycoon Mohamad "Bob" Hasan with 20 percent, an Indonesian army pension fund with 25 percent and Mandala Putra's Humpuss Group with 15 percent.
Mandala Putra said the airline hoped to raise between 250 billion and 350 billion rupiah in the float to improve its capital structure.

The old management was successful enough in marketing and promotion but the company's financial performance was felt to be less than efficient and did not meet expectations, he said without elaborating.
Sempati's shares would be sold after the company was truly healthy so investors would not be disappointed, he added.
"We will sell shares in the capital market only if the company is truly healthy so that investors will not lose," he said.
While Mandala Putra said investors from Singapore and Malaysia had shown interest in the airline, there was sufficient domestic interest for a local listing.
"We will give priority to selling shares on the exchange as the domestic market's potential is big enough," he said.
Nainggolan was quoted as saying the change of directors meant the 1997 float target could still be met.

Antara said the management reshuffle also included a new director of finance, I Cenik Ardana, operations director, Captain Boedi Rahardjo, commercial director, Arie Johanes Toelle, and general affairs director, Suroso Wening.
Sempati flies mostly domestic routes with international services to Australia, Malaysia, Singapore and Taiwan.
